page: Microsoft Azure E16ds_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Edsv7 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes a 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is bundled with a 945 GB local disk, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core scoring 2284.59, placing it in the top 25% of tested systems. Single-threaded compression and decompression tasks show top-tier performance, with gzip compression reaching 36.52 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 15.37 GB/sec, both in the top 10%. Multi-core CPU performance is average, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 18622.51 and a PassMark CPU score of 31315.04. Memory bandwidth is also average, measuring 1377.27 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 136.15 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. For LLM inference, the server achieves a top-tier text generation speed of 343.48 tokens/sec on a small 135M model, though prompt processing speeds and larger model execution remain in the average tier.

The E16ds_v7 offers high resource density for memory-intensive workloads without the overhead of a GPU. The inclusion of a 945 GB local disk and Premium Storage capability provides a balanced storage-to-memory profile, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring high RAM capacity and local scratch space. The dedicated CPU allocation and advanced instruction sets, such as AVX-512 and AMX, support accelerated vector and matrix operations. This server is suited for relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, data analytics, and memory-bound enterprise applications.
